text: The battlefield consists of the two rows you can see below.
The lower row for your party, the upper for the enemies.
The [FIREBRICK]red[BLACK] spaces on the upper row indicate your attack range.
Each turn, you get a certain amount of Action Points (AP).
With these AP, you can move, attack, or do other actions.
Advantage greatly increases your hit and critical hit chance,
while disadvantage greatly decreases it, along with your damage.
Each enemy has an [BLUE]advantage[BLACK] ([BLUE]+[BLACK]) and a [FIREBRICK]disadvantage[BLACK] ([FIREBRICK]-[BLACK])
against specific weapon types, such as a sword type or an axe type.
Try to use the right weapon type against each enemy.
[FIREBRICK]BEWARE![BLACK] When you have a disadvantage with your weapon against
an enemy, it means that the enemy has an advantage against you!
At the start of each turn, if a character begins
next to an enemy, they become locked in battle.
This is marked by a small [GOLD]yellow[BLACK] exclamation mark [!].
This [BLUE]significantly[BLACK] increases the AP cost to move
away from that enemy and escape the battle lock.
The Stealth skill reduces the AP cost to escape battle lock.
When you end your turn, any AP you did not
spend can be added to your next turn's AP.
Each 10 ranks in [BLUE]Stamina[BLACK] lets you
carry over 1 more AP.
For now, with your current attributes,
it means you can have a maximum of 5 AP.
At the top of the screen, you can see the turn order.
It shows the upcoming turns from left to right, with
the currently acting character highlighted on the left.
The turn order is based on the [BLUE]Speed[BLACK] attribute.
Each party member's speed is shown in the
bottom-right corner of their turn icon.
A faster character acts more often.
The amount of visible spaces in the turn order
is only at 3 now. But as your party grows, more
spaces will become visible.
Specific items will also increase this amount.
It is possible that you have acquired a magic spell by now.
If so, you can use it in the battle menu under [BLUE]Special[BLACK].
Remember, magic spells require resources to cast.
Weapons and shields have limited [BLUE]durability[BLACK].
You can see their durability in parentheses after
the items' names. Each use reduces durability by 1.
When durability reaches [FIREBRICK]0[BLACK], the item breaks and is [FIREBRICK]lost[BLACK].
Always monitor your weapons' durability to avoid surprises!
The Mechanic skill gives your party the ability to repair items.
Enemies will try to choose their target based on the most
damage they can deal. Weaker, less protected heroes, with no
advantage, and within range, are more likely to be targeted.
The Stealth skill however, helps to make a hero less likely
to be targeted by enemies.
